title: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment.…
content: “But here, Udāyi, a person thinks: ‘Attachment is the source of suffering.’ Having known this, he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. Udāyi, I say: ‘This person is not bound, not fettered.’ Why is that? Udāyi, the difference in his faculties has been fully understood by me.”

title: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or…
content: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old — aged, bent like a roof, crooked, leaning on a staff, trembling as she walks, sick, her youth exhausted, teeth broken, hair grey, bald, wrinkled, limbs shriveled and pale. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

title: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” -…
content: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Brahmin, being infatuated by craving, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both, and experiences mental suffering and mental distress. When craving is abandoned, one does not plan for one’s own harm, nor for others’ harm, nor for the harm of both, and does not experience mental suffering or mental distress. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one engages in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. When craving is abandoned, one does not engage in misconduct of body, speech, or mind. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one does not know as it actually is one’s own benefit, nor the benefit of others, nor the benefit of both. When craving is abandoned, one knows as it actually is one’s own benefit, the benefit of others, and the benefit of both. Thus, brahmin, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — A collection of many diseases, impure, Full of stench, rotting. Develop your mind, Contemplate the…
content:
Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
A collection of many diseases, impure,
Full of stench, rotting.
Develop your mind,
Contemplate the nature of foulness,
Achieve one-pointedness,
With mind well concentrated.

Practice the signless,
Abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.
By fully understanding conceit,
You will live at peace.

title: “That is so, great king. Few are those in the world who, having obtained abundant, great wealth, do not become infatuated, do not become intoxicated,…
content:
“That is so, great king. Few are those in the world who, having obtained abundant, great wealth, do not become infatuated, do not become intoxicated, do not fall into heedlessness regarding sensual pleasures, and do not act wrongly toward others. But many are those in the world who, having obtained abundant, great wealth, become infatuated, intoxicated, fall into heedlessness regarding sensual pleasures, and act wrongly toward others.

Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures,
People are greedy and deluded,
In the midst of sensual pleasures,
Without clear awareness,
They are overly intoxicated,
Like a deer unaware of the trap set —
Later they suffer,
Experiencing the results of evil deeds.”

title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk does not delight in…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk does not delight in those forms, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then that monk is called one who has not swallowed Māra’s hook, who has broken the hook, destroyed the hook, who has not fallen into misfortune, into calamity, not subject to the Evil One’s will. There are sounds … odors … tastes … touches … phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk does not delight in those phenomena, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then that monk is called one who has not swallowed Māra’s hook, who has broken the hook, destroyed the hook, who has not fallen into misfortune, into calamity, not subject to the Evil One’s will.”

title: Elder Māṇava: “I saw an old person, I saw a sick person in pain, I saw a dead person, With life exhausted — Therefore I…
content:
Elder Māṇava:
“I saw an old person,
I saw a sick person in pain,
I saw a dead person,
With life exhausted —
Therefore I went forth,
Leaving the home life,
Abandoning sensual pleasures
That are enticing and agreeable.”

title: The Blessed One replied to Piṅgiya: “Seeing the danger in all forms, Beings living heedlessly, Afflicted by forms — Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.…
content:
The Blessed One replied to Piṅgiya:
“Seeing the danger in all forms,
Beings living heedlessly,
Afflicted by forms —
Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.
Abandon forms so as not to come to birth again.

Seeing beings, human folk,
Falling into craving,
Burned by old age,
Overcome by old age —
Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.
Abandon craving so as not to come to birth again.”

title: Suffering from disease and aging, And also subject to death — Such is the nature of conditioned things, Such is the nature of beings. If…
content:
Suffering from disease and aging,
And also subject to death —
Such is the nature of conditioned things,
Such is the nature of beings.
If ordinary people become disenchanted,
That would not be fitting for me —
If I too were disenchanted
With beings who share the same fate.
While I live,
Not different from them,
I dwell thus,
Knowing the Dhamma without attachment.
Conceit in health,
In youth, in life —
All these I have subdued,
Springing from security.
I see the path of seclusion,
I arouse strong energy,
Seeing the state of Nibbāna.
Now I cannot
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
I will not fall back,
Achieving the final goal of the holy life.

title: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied…
content: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because form is suffering, Mahāli, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings become disenchanted with form. Through disenchantment, they become dispassionate; through dispassion, they are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are purified. If feeling … perception … formations … if consciousness were exclusively happiness … beings would not become disenchanted with consciousness. But because consciousness is suffering … beings become disenchanted with consciousness … and are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings.”
